html:
In the app

File → New Project… → A graded level → 11. Guided mode opens on this chapter: the tags, every rung below under its fold, a Verify check, and the run results: the marker carries its message, a bottle is marked, a bottle of the second lot carries L0102, then complete, every bottle right and under par. File → Load Reference Solution loads the program printed here.

Every bottle that leaves a plant carries a code: the lot it came from, so a complaint can be traced back to a tank and a day. Printing it is one machine’s job and reading it back is another’s, because a printer that has stopped printing does not know it has. Level 11 is Level 8’s line with a laser marker in front of the camera. The marker writes the lot code on each bottle as it passes; the camera, on a code-verify job, reads it back and tells you whether it is there and whether it is the right lot. Three lots of six bottles go through, and the lot changes while bottles are still on the belt. The traps are all in the handshakes: the marker’s message, the camera’s expectation, and keeping each bottle’s lot with the bottle.

The marker

The Date Coder part under Bottling is a CO2 laser marker by default (an inkjet is the other option; its I/O

differs only in the service signal). It marks the bottle under its head when Print rises, and only while Laser_On arms it: that is the marker’s interlock, and a Mark with the laser disarmed does nothing but a line in the log. Its message is L, the four-digit lot, a dash and a running count: L0101-001. The lot comes from Lot_No, but writing Lot_No changes nothing by itself: the message is loaded on the rising edge of Load_Msg, the load takes half a second with Ready off, and Msg_Ready comes on when the message carries the lot Lot_No holds. A mark is missed now and then (the bottle rocked), and after ten marks the protective window has fumed up: Window_Dirty comes on and every other mark comes out faint until the window is cleaned. The head’s own eye, Detect, says a bottle is under it.

The camera’s code-verify job

The camera runs Bottle code verify: cap, label and fill as before, and the code read back by OCR. Two result bits are new: 32, wrong lot code: the camera read a code, but not the lot it was told to expect; 64, no code: nothing readable, a missed mark, a faint one or a bottle that was never marked. The lot the camera should expect comes from the PLC in User_Data bytes 0-1, latched with Set_User_Data ahead of each trigger, the way Level 9 passed its batch data. Tell it nothing and it checks nothing: every code reads as right, and a bottle with the wrong lot ships. The string it read comes back in Inspection_Results bytes 12-27 (NOREAD when there was nothing), and Camera_HMI shows it.

How the level is scored

What happensPoints
A bottle in Good_Bin that is good and carries its own lot code+100
What happensPoints
A defective bottle in Reject_Bin (cap, label, fill, no code, wrong lot code)+100
A bottle shipped with a defect, no code or the wrong lot code−100
A good bottle rejected−50
All eighteen bottles done under par (45 s)+200

The lot a bottle should carry is the lot the selector showed when it left the hopper. A bottle marked with the lot of the batch before or after it is wrong even if the camera, told the wrong thing, let it through. The Coder record line in the simulator log at the end counts marks, misses, faint marks, marks with no bottle and marks with the laser disarmed.

Three handshakes and two FIFOs

The selector tells you the lot of the next bottle out of the hopper. The bottle under the marker left the hopper 2.5 s ago, and the bottle under the camera a second before that: at a lot change there are bottles of the old lot on the belt when the selector already shows the new one. So the lot has to travel with the bottle, and the program does that the way Level 8 carried result codes: a FIFO from the hopper to the marker (Lot_Q), loaded with the selector’s lot at each release and unloaded as each bottle reaches the marker’s eye, and a second FIFO from the marker to the camera (Cam_Q). Then three handshakes: the marker’s message load, the camera’s user data, and the camera’s trigger and results, which are Level 8’s.

One more thing the FIFO gives you: its head, Lot_Q[0], is the lot of the next bottle to reach the marker. The program hands the marker that lot as soon as it changes, while the bottle is still on its way, so the half-second load is over before the bottle arrives. Load it on arrival instead and the bottle is past the head before Msg_Ready returns.

Run it

Load the program, Run mode, Start. The marker loads L0101 before the first bottle reaches it (the FIFO head is set at the first release), marks the first six, and the moment the sixth has been marked the FIFO head reads 102 and the log shows loading message L0102. 18 of 18 bottles in the right bin, nothing lost, in about 36 s against a par of 45 s: 2000 points and three stars.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: the seal-in

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run (Seal-in run bit) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: The belt and the run lamp follow Run
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns Conveyor_Run (Belt motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Conveyor_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conveyor_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: CAMERA SETUP: triggering enabled, results buffered

pred.q: E_Stop is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable is off and Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable is off. It stops at XIC(E_Stop).

rungs.words: When E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: LASER: armed while the line runs. The marker's interlock: with Laser_On off a Mark does nothing
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns Laser_On (Laser marker: arm the laser (its interlock); no mark while 0) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. OTE(Laser_On) Output Energize does: turns Laser_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: THE LOT: the selector says which lot the NEXT bottle out of the hopper belongs to. The bottles already on the belt belong to the lot they were released under, so a lot rides with its bottle in the FIFOs below

pred.q: Lot_101 is off and Lot_103 is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: Power reaches only part of the rung: Lot_Want is not written (it keeps its value), Lot_Want is written and Lot_Want is not written (it keeps its value).

rungs.words: Each path is tested on its own: if Lot_101 (Lot selector at 101 (left)) is on, it puts 101 into Lot_Want (The lot the selector shows: the lot of the next bottle to be released); if Lot_101 is off and Lot_103 (Lot selector at 103 (right); neither = 102) is off, it puts 102 into Lot_Want; if Lot_103 is on, it puts 103 into Lot_Want.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Lot_101) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lot_101 is on.
    2. MOV(101,Lot_Want) Move does: puts 101 into Lot_Want. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Lot_101) Examine If Open asks: true when Lot_101 is off.
    2. XIO(Lot_103) Examine If Open asks: true when Lot_103 is off.
    3. MOV(102,Lot_Want) Move does: puts 102 into Lot_Want. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Lot_103) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lot_103 is on.
    2. MOV(103,Lot_Want) Move does: puts 103 into Lot_Want. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: RELEASE: a bottle every 0.9 s while the hopper exit is clear
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, Infeed_Ready (Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released) is on and Rel_T.DN (the done bit of Rel_T: Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s) is off, the rung runs the timer Rel_T (Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s) toward 900 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Infeed_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Ready is on.
  3. XIO(Rel_T.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when Rel_T.DN is off.
  4. TON(Rel_T,900,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Rel_T toward 900 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Rel_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: One scan of Infeed_Release is one bottle; its lot goes into the hopper-to-marker FIFO in the same scan
rungs.words: When Rel_T.DN (the done bit of Rel_T: Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s) is on, the rung turns Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and loads Lot_Want (The lot the selector shows: the lot of the next bottle to be released) into the queue Lot_Q[0] (The lots of the bottles between the hopper and the marker, oldest first).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Rel_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Rel_T.DN is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Infeed_Release) Output Energize does: turns Infeed_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. FFL(Lot_Want,Lot_Q[0],Lot_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Load does: loads Lot_Want into the queue Lot_Q[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.why: Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.
pats.think: a ticket roll at a deli counter: the first ticket torn off is the first one served.
pats.watch: A load and an unload must happen once per part each. A part that leaves the line between the two (a reject, a part picked off) has to be unloaded too, or every answer after it belongs to the wrong part.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: MARKER MESSAGE: Lot_Q[0] is the lot of the next bottle to reach the marker, so the marker is told its lot while the bottle is still on its way (2.5 s). Lot_No alone changes nothing: the message is loaded on Load_Msg
rungs.words: When Lot_Q_Ctl.POS (the position of Lot_Q_Ctl: FIFO control for Lot_Q) is greater than 0 and Coder_Lot (Laser marker: the lot number for the message) is not Lot_Q[0] (The lots of the bottles between the hopper and the marker, oldest first), the rung puts Lot_Q[0] into Coder_Lot.
rungs.ltr:
1. GRT(Lot_Q_Ctl.POS,0) Greater Than asks: true when Lot_Q_Ctl.POS is greater than 0.
  2. NEQ(Coder_Lot,Lot_Q[0]) Not Equal asks: true when Coder_Lot is not Lot_Q[0].
  3. MOV(Lot_Q[0],Coder_Lot) Move does: puts Lot_Q[0] into Coder_Lot. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: Load the message once whenever it does not carry Lot_No: a rising edge of Load_Msg, half a second with the marker not ready, then Msg_Ready
rungs.words: When Coder_Lot (Laser marker: the lot number for the message) is greater than 0, Coder_Msg_Ready (Laser marker: the message carries Lot_No) is off, Coder_Ready (Laser marker ready: armed and not loading) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Coder_Load (Laser marker: load Lot_No into the message (rising edge, 0.5 s)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. GRT(Coder_Lot,0) Greater Than asks: true when Coder_Lot is greater than 0.
  2. XIO(Coder_Msg_Ready) Examine If Open asks: true when Coder_Msg_Ready is off.
  3. XIC(Coder_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Coder_Ready is on.
  4. ONS(Load_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Load_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  5. OTE(Coder_Load) Output Energize does: turns Coder_Load on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: AT THE MARKER: a bottle arrives; the oldest lot in the FIFO is its lot. Unload it into Mark_Lot and pass it on to the marker-to-camera FIFO
rungs.words: When PE_Coder (The marker head's eye: a bottle is under the head) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung unloads the oldest entry of Lot_Q[0] (The lots of the bottles between the hopper and the marker, oldest first) into Mark_Lot (The lot of the bottle at the marker: what its message must carry) and loads Mark_Lot into the queue Cam_Q[0] (The lots of the bottles between the marker and the camera, oldest first).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Coder) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Coder is on.
  2. ONS(Mark_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Mark_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. FFU(Lot_Q[0],Mark_Lot,Lot_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Unload does: unloads the oldest entry of Lot_Q[0] into Mark_Lot. One entry per false-to-true transition.
    Path 2
    1. FFL(Mark_Lot,Cam_Q[0],Cam_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Load does: loads Mark_Lot into the queue Cam_Q[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: MARK: a bottle under the head, the message loaded and carrying this bottle's lot: Mark rises and the laser writes it. A bottle that arrives while the message is still loading is not marked (the camera will see no code and reject it), so the lot has to be sent ahead, as the rung above does

pred.q: PE_Coder is on, Coder_Msg_Ready is off, Coder_Lot is 47 and Mark_Lot is 48. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Coder_Mark is off. It stops at XIC(Coder_Msg_Ready).

rungs.words: When PE_Coder (The marker head's eye: a bottle is under the head) is on, Coder_Msg_Ready (Laser marker: the message carries Lot_No) is on and Coder_Lot (Laser marker: the lot number for the message) equals Mark_Lot (The lot of the bottle at the marker: what its message must carry), the rung turns Coder_Mark (Laser marker: mark the message on the bottle under the head (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Coder) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Coder is on.
  2. XIC(Coder_Msg_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Coder_Msg_Ready is on.
  3. EQU(Coder_Lot,Mark_Lot) Equal asks: true when Coder_Lot equals Mark_Lot. Both values are compared every scan.
  4. OTE(Coder_Mark) Output Energize does: turns Coder_Mark on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: A BOTTLE AT THE CAMERA: remember that it wants an inspection, and take its lot out of the marker-to-camera FIFO
rungs.words: When PE_Trigger (Presence eye at the camera: a bottle is in the field of view) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches Trig_Req (A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection) on and unloads the oldest entry of Cam_Q[0] (The lots of the bottles between the marker and the camera, oldest first) into Cam_Lot (The lot the camera should read on the bottle it is about to inspect).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Trigger) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Trigger is on.
  2. ONS(Trig_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Trig_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Trig_Req) Output Latch does: latches Trig_Req on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. FFU(Cam_Q[0],Cam_Lot,Cam_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Unload does: unloads the oldest entry of Cam_Q[0] into Cam_Lot. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.why: Trig_Req stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: USER DATA first: the lot the camera should read on this bottle, bytes 0-1, then Set_User_Data
rungs.words: When Trig_Req (A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection) is on and Cam1:O.Set_User_Data is off, the rung copies 2 elements from Cam_Lot (The lot the camera should read on the bottle it is about to inspect) to Cam1:O.User_Data[0] and latches Cam1:O.Set_User_Data on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Trig_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Trig_Req is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Set_User_Data) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Set_User_Data is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. COP(Cam_Lot,Cam1:O.User_Data[0],2) Copy File does: copies 2 elements from Cam_Lot to Cam1:O.User_Data[0].
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Set_User_Data) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Set_User_Data on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Set_User_Data stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.comment: TRIGGER once the camera has the lot and is ready
rungs.words: When Trig_Req (A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection) is on, Cam1:I.Set_User_Data_Ack is on and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on, the rung latches Cam1:O.Trigger on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Trig_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Trig_Req is on.
  2. XIC(Cam1:I.Set_User_Data_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Set_User_Data_Ack is on.
  3. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on.
  4. OTL(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Trigger on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Trigger stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: Acknowledged: drop the trigger and the data request

pred.q: Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Cam1:O.Trigger is unlatched, Trig_Req is unlatched and Cam1:O.Set_User_Data is unlatched.

rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger, unlatches Trig_Req (A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection) and unlatches Cam1:O.Set_User_Data.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Trig_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Trig_Req. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Cam1:O.Set_User_Data) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Set_User_Data. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Trigger when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: A RESULT: its code into the FIFO (bits 0-2 cap, label, fill; 32 wrong lot code; 64 no code) and the acknowledge
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off, the rung loads Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into the queue Res_Q[0] (The result codes between the camera and the reject pusher, oldest first) and latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. FFL(Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code,Res_Q[0],Res_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Load does: loads Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into the queue Res_Q[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 16
rungs.comment: Results_Valid down: ack down

pred.q: Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is left as it was. It stops at XIO(Cam1:I.Results_Valid).

rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off.
  2. OTU(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 17
rungs.comment: AT THE REJECT PUSHER: the oldest result is this bottle's
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung unloads the oldest entry of Res_Q[0] (The result codes between the camera and the reject pusher, oldest first) into Cur (The result code of the bottle at the reject pusher).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. FFU(Res_Q[0],Cur,Res_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Unload does: unloads the oldest entry of Res_Q[0] into Cur. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 18
rungs.comment: Any defect bit, the code bits included: arm the pusher
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on, this is the first scan of it and Cur (The result code of the bottle at the reject pusher) is not 0, the rung latches Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS2) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS2). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. NEQ(Cur,0) Not Equal asks: true when Cur is not 0.
  4. OTL(Fire) Output Latch does: latches Fire on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Fire stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 19
rungs.comment: Push while the bottle is at the eye
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) is on, the rung turns Reject (Reject pusher cylinder) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
  3. OTE(Reject) Output Energize does: turns Reject on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 20
rungs.comment: Count it
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: if Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) is on, it makes Reject_Count (Shown on the toolbar: bottles you rejected) = Reject_Count + 1; if Fire is off, it makes Pass_Count (Shown on the toolbar: bottles you let through) = Pass_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Cnt_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Cnt_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
    2. ADD(Reject_Count,1,Reject_Count) Add does: makes Reject_Count = Reject_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Fire) Examine If Open asks: true when Fire is off.
    2. ADD(Pass_Count,1,Pass_Count) Add does: makes Pass_Count = Pass_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 21
rungs.comment: The bottle has gone: disarm
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is off, the rung unlatches Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(PE_Reject) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Reject is off.
  2. OTU(Fire) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fire. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Fire when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 22
rungs.comment: WINDOW: the lamp calls the operator; three seconds after it lights the window is cleaned. Without the lamp every other mark stays faint and goes to the reject bin

pred.q: Window_Dirty is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Lamp_Lens is on.

rungs.words: When Window_Dirty (Laser marker: the protective window has fumed up, marks come out faint) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Lens (Window lamp: tells the operator to clean the laser window) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Window_Dirty) Examine If Closed asks: true when Window_Dirty is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Lens) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Lens on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 23
rungs.comment: FAULT LAMP: a lost result, a missed trigger, the camera off line
rungs.words: When either (Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is on), (Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on) or (Cam1:I.Online is off), the rung turns Lamp_Fault (Fault lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Missed_Acq) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIO(Cam1:I.Online) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Online is off.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Infeed_Ready.desc: Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released

Rel_T.desc: Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s

Infeed_Release.desc: Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)

Lot_Q.desc: The lots of the bottles between the hopper and the marker, oldest first

Coder_Lot.desc: Laser marker: the lot number for the message

Coder_Msg_Ready.desc: Laser marker: the message carries Lot_No

Coder_Ready.desc: Laser marker ready: armed and not loading

Load_ONS.desc: One-shot storage for the message load

Coder_Load.desc: Laser marker: load Lot_No into the message (rising edge, 0.5 s)

PE_Coder.desc: The marker head's eye: a bottle is under the head

Mark_Lot.desc: The lot of the bottle at the marker: what its message must carry

Cam_Q.desc: The lots of the bottles between the marker and the camera, oldest first

Coder_Mark.desc: Laser marker: mark the message on the bottle under the head (rising edge)

PE_Trigger.desc: Presence eye at the camera: a bottle is in the field of view

Trig_Req.desc: A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection

Cam_Lot.desc: The lot the camera should read on the bottle it is about to inspect

Res_Q.desc: The result codes between the camera and the reject pusher, oldest first

PE_Reject.desc: Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher

Cur.desc: The result code of the bottle at the reject pusher

Fire.desc: Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected

Reject_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: bottles you rejected

Pass_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: bottles you let through

Window_Dirty.desc: Laser marker: the protective window has fumed up, marks come out faint

Lamp_Lens.desc: Window lamp: tells the operator to clean the laser window
